summary: The 8-week migration from Hive to a Delta Lakehouse on Databricks establishes a scalable, ACID-compliant architecture with unified batch and streaming analytics. The program promises 50% faster queries, improved data integrity, and 30% storage savings. Core deliverables include Hive table conversion, ETL modernization, BI dashboard continuity, and Unity Catalog governance—all planned within the existing $80K monthly compute budget.
scope_overview: Migration encompasses 500+ tables (200TB), 150 Airflow ETL jobs, and 50 BI dashboards. Deliverables include Delta conversion, ACID enablement, time-travel setup (30-day retention), Z-order performance optimization, and Unity Catalog integration to achieve consistent, governed, real-time analytics across Databricks Runtime 13.3 LTS on AWS.
key_risks: Potential dashboard downtime during phased table conversions impacting business reporting.
Query optimization may fall short of the 50% improvement target if Z-order columns are misidentified.
test_readiness: QA reports strong readiness with automated tests covering API behavior, schema validation, concurrent write integrity, Z-order performance, governance, streaming resilience, and workshop evaluations. Staging mirrors production environment, ensuring comprehensive regression and performance validation prior to rollout.
recommendations: Perform early profiling of query patterns to fine-tune Z-order column selection and ensure KPI achievement.
Conduct phased migration using shadow tables and adopt a staggered dashboard switch to eliminate downtime.
next_steps: Complete high-priority Hive-to-Delta conversions and validate key BI dashboards in staging.
Initiate performance benchmarking and governance rollout via Unity Catalog before full production cutover.
